title: Data.gov catalog
description: The U.S. government's open data catalog, with datasets published by federal agencies.
content: Explore public datasets by topic, agency, and location. Catalog records point to source agencies and describe formats, update schedules, and access conditions.

title: Library of Congress digital collections
description: Search digitized photographs, maps, manuscripts, newspapers, sound recordings, and other collection materials.
content: Collection pages provide descriptions and access to digitized primary sources. Item records may include dates, creators, subjects, formats, and rights information.

title: National Archives Catalog
description: Search descriptions of records held by the U.S. National Archives and participating institutions.
content: Catalog entries describe records, archival creators, series, and digitized objects. Search result metadata can help trace provenance and identify records for further review.
source: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration

title: Climate Data Online
description: Discover historical weather and climate data products from NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information.
content: The catalog covers station observations and other climate records. Dataset descriptions and station metadata are important when comparing locations, time spans, and measurement methods.

title: NASA Earth Observatory
description: Earth science stories and imagery about the planet's land, oceans, atmosphere, and changing climate.
content: Articles explain observations from satellite instruments and other sources, with context about dates, locations, and environmental processes. Images and captions link observations to source missions.

title: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program
description: Earthquake information, hazard resources, maps, and data from the U.S. Geological Survey.
content: The program publishes earthquake event information and explanatory material about hazards and seismic monitoring. Event records can include time, magnitude, location, and review status.

title: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
description: Guidance for organizations to understand, assess, prioritize, and communicate cybersecurity risk.
content: The framework organizes cybersecurity outcomes and references. It is intended to support risk management across organizations rather than prescribe a single technical implementation.
source: National Institute of Standards and Technology

title: Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog
description: CISA's catalog of vulnerabilities known to have been exploited in the wild.
content: Catalog records include vulnerability identifiers, product and vendor details, action guidance, and due dates for federal agencies under binding operational directives. The entries are useful for prioritization, not a complete vulnerability inventory.

title: SEC EDGAR company filings
description: Search filings submitted to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission by public companies and other filers.
content: EDGAR filing records identify issuers, filing types, and submission dates. Company filings are primary disclosures and should be read in their filing context, including amendments and exhibits.

title: PubMed biomedical literature search
description: Search citations and abstracts for biomedical and life sciences literature.
content: PubMed records include bibliographic details and links to available full text. Indexing and publication metadata help narrow a literature search but do not replace assessment of study design or evidence quality.

title: EPA Envirofacts data access
description: EPA tools for exploring environmental information and datasets from agency programs.
content: Environmental records may describe facilities, regulated activities, and measurements. Interpret records with the associated program definitions, geographic coverage, and reporting dates.

title: NASA Earthdata search
description: Find Earth science data products and information from NASA's Earth-observing missions.
content: Earthdata resources describe data products, mission instruments, and access pathways. Product metadata can help compare spatial coverage, temporal resolution, and processing levels across observations.
